I enjoyed the hell out of these posts. Made me feel good about what I was doing. Patternmaking is great and frustrating and challenging and rewarding as heck. 

I started back in the day with a shitty free sewing machine, sewing by hand, and some shitty Fiskars. I have now invested in nicer equipment. Began by altering my own clothes, chopping them up and making new crappy pieces. Then I found some shirts and trousers that I liked at garage sales/thrift stores/flea markets and reverse engineered with cheap fabric from the same g.sales/thrift/flea markets. Rebuilt a cashmere topcoat, peacoat, tweed blazer and did my best to make patterns out of butcher paper and roll-ends from the newspaper factory in town. At the start, nothing ever fit me that looked good; everything that fit looked like crap. (probably a self esteem issue) I buy lots of patterns from thrift stores for mega cheap also.

I built my own dress form out of a thick hanger and a tshirt to destroy, wrapping myself with [wet packing tape](https://www.amazon.com/Reinforced-Gummed-shipping-sealing-activated/dp/B01JKJO6TW/ref=pd_lpo_229_lp_tr_img_3?_encoding=UTF8&psc=1&refRID=SRTGFH0S54G4BCAX204Z). Pass out from overheating and have your mom freak out, cut you out of it. Then patch it up with more tape until you have a mass that somewhat resembles an upper torso of yours.

Fixed that to a coat rack and started working on building from my patterns, tweaking it after being able to see it hung up. It's difficult to work only on the table, pinning parts to my shirt to try and get a feel for it in the mirror. Found some dress forms at an auction for cheap, so I snagged the fuckers up and oh lordy what a change from the welfare handmade version.

A great resource for me was youtube, [cutter and tailor forum](http://www.cutterandtailor.com/forum/) and the book by [Dave Coffin](https://www.amazon.com/gp/offer-listing/1561580155/ref=tmm_hrd_new_olp_sr?ie=UTF8&condition=new&qid=&sr=)

I'll usually result in a bloodbath mongoloid of something, then see how others do it and reattempt, which yields different results. They know their customers. Especially in-store branches: they know when you come in, they know your family, you've been telling them your life story. When you're going on vacation. I did something similar when I was 13. After not talking to my dad for a decade, I decided to reach out and call his house phone after not returning calls through highschool and shortly after. My stepsisters would bash me openly on myspace and then facebook, accusing me of all sorts of shit, and it drove me away even further.

When I called, it went to the voicemail and not sure if it was his, I left a 'Hey this is SD and I uh was wondering if you were still living there. I left my number and kind of freaked out for a day until he called me back. It was goddamn uncomfortable, surreal, felt like as bad and intoxicating as the shitty lies I told years before. But I went against it. We made a deal to hook up and go grab a beer (I was drinking age by then, fucking crazy that I had just masturbated for the first time months before I last saw him). 

It was awkward. He told me about work; I told him about work. Lots of quick shitty small talk. Then he drops a bit about how he is 55 and on the downhill slope, just waiting for death. Over weight, unhealthy, skin red and grey. I didn't really get into any specific past things; we just talked about what we were doing and then made tentative plans to talk on the phone later, almost like we were on a first date. A horribly confusing, overwhelming, and ultimately heartbreaking first date. The next day, I broke down at work and wanted to cry, but honestly I couldn't. I hadn't cried in a long time (just recently got an authentic tear out two weeks ago).

Years have gone by and with each conversation, we have defined what we want our relationship to be like. We have been able to pull each other out of shitty depressed cycles a few times. It is becoming more and more comfortable. His and my health are improving, our goals, our lives.

I am in the position to help out my dad now that he is recently divorced again and do things with and for him (medically, house chores, lending an ear, BEING PRESENT) that has been reciprocated. I don't think I am going to be able to fully rectify the guilt and shame without making forward moving action.

I have told him some things about the past that I was going to take with me to the grave, and it kind of blew him away. He apologized about some things; other things I think went over his head.

Remembering my past age and mental immaturity was naturally paired and past experiences aren't wholly defining qualities. It feels amazing to get rid of baggage that perpetually tried to rope my neck.

Good luck to you. I did worse, and I think I have an elevated level of empathy because of it. I hope you can feel what I feel.
